This section presents an empirical analysis addressing central aspects of our approach: the quality of generated training data, the impact of context window size, and the effect of model scaling. # 6.1 Quality Analysis of Synthesized Data To rigorously evaluate the quality of data generated by DeepForge, we constructed multiple SFT training sets with different sizes. These datasets were used to train the Qwen3-8B model, and model performance was evaluated on the BrowseComp-ZH benchmark. For comparison, we use SFT-only versions of WebExplorer-8B (trained on 13k samples) and DeepDive-9B (trained on 858 samples) as our baselines. Figure 4 shows that accuracy scales steadily with dataset size. Notably, with only 2k samples, our model achieves $19.7\%$ accuracy, substantially outperforming DeepDive-9B (15.7% with 858 samples). This highlights the high quality and efficiency of data generated by DeepForge. # 6.2 Effect of Different Context Window Sizes To assess how context length influences the performance of deep research models, we systematically evaluate OffSeeker across GAIA and BrowseComp-ZH, under context windows from 16k to 128k tokens. As illustrated in Figure 5, accuracy increases consistently with larger context windows. On GAIA, performance rises from $33.98\%$ at 16k to $56.31\%$ at 128k. The effect is even more pronounced on the more demanding BrowseComp-ZH benchmark, where accuracy improves from $3.48\%$ to $29.97\%$ . Notably, a 32k context window yields only about $35\%$ of the performance achieved with the 128k setting. These findings underscore the critical role of extended context capacity in enabling complex, multi-hop reasoning and the integration of dispersed evidence, capabilities essential for advanced research-oriented tasks. To study the effect of model scaling, we compare OffSeeker of varying sizes (4B, 8B, and 14B parameters), trained on DeepForge-Dataset based on the Qwen3 series of models [30], and evaluate their performance on GAIA and BrowseComp-ZH. # 6.3 Effect of Model Scaling Effect of Model Scaling. As shown in Table 4, accuracy consistently improves as model size increases. The largest model, OffSeeker-14B (SFT), achieves $51.4\%$ and $24.6\%$ on GAIA and BrowseComp-ZH, respectively. Applying DPO training yields additional gains across all sizes; OffSeeker-14B with DPO reaches $54.4\%$ on GAIA and $27.0\%$ on BrowseComp-ZH, highlighting the effectiveness of offline DPO.
